messages:
Alex R: Quick thread — ran multi-GPU inference benchmarks comparing PCIe vs SXM node topologies across regions. Sharing quick findings and the harness/flags we used. Want sanity-checks on NVLink behavior and NUMA pinning notes.

Jin W: Nice. Which models and kernel stack? short summary plz.

Alex R: Models: gpt-j-6B (baseline) and opt-13b-trim (13B). Sequence len 1024, typical prompt size ~64, generation 256 tokens. Harness: perfbench v2 (internal) with streaming disabled, synchronous latency-first runs and a separate throughput sweep.
Command (example):
```
perfbench --model opt-13b-trim --device multi-gpu --gpus 4 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --concurrency 16 --kernels cutlass,flash_attn --numactl-bind=0,1 --mode throughput
```

Olga P: Perf numbers? are you comparing same instance types (vCPU, PCIe lanes)?

perf-bot: Auto-run summary (all runs seed-locked, stable clocks):
- us-west1 A100 PCIe (4x A100 PCIe, 96 vCPU): per-GPU p50=28ms p95=120ms p99=240ms, throughput per GPU=420 tok/s, 4-GPU aggregate throughput=1600 tok/s.
- us-west1 A100 SXM (4x A100-SXM NVLink, 96 vCPU): per-GPU p50=22ms p95=95ms p99=180ms, throughput per GPU=520 tok/s, 4-GPU aggregate throughput=2080 tok/s.
- eu-central1 A100 SXM (4x A100-SXM, different host interconnect): per-GPU p50=24ms p95=110ms p99=200ms, throughput per GPU=490 tok/s.

Samira G: Interesting. So SXM gives ~20-25% boost per GPU mostly due to NVLink?

Alex R: Yes. Key points from traces: NVLink peer-to-peer reduced inter-GPU KV-cache exchange time by ~35ms on avg for 4-GPU sharded attention. On PCIe nodes we saw higher variance — p95 driven by bus contention when multiple GPUs exchanged large KV chunks.

Jin W: Did you try NUMA pinning (numactl) and CPU affinity? I've seen big wins when CPU-GPU affinity is tight on PCIe boxes.

perf-bot: NUMA tuning results (us-west1 A100 PCIe):
- default: p95=120ms (as above)
- with numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 and pinned worker threads: p95=105ms (12.5% improvement), p50 unchanged.

Olga P: That matches our past infra notes. On SXM nodes the benefit was smaller (p95 improved ~6%) because NVLink reduces cross-host traffic and the driver already schedules better.

Alex R: Kernel choices: we compared cutlass (optimized GEMM paths), flash_attn kernels, and a Triton-backed fused attention. On SXM, cutlass+flash_attn had best throughput for fp16 regressed runs. On PCIe, Triton fusion reduced CPU->GPU transfer overhead for small micro-batches and improved p50 by ~6% but throughput stayed ~5-8% lower than cutlass on SXM.

perf-bot: Kernel summary (opt-13b, fp16):
- cutlass+flash_attn (SXM): 520 tok/s per GPU
- triton-fused (PCIe): 390 tok/s per GPU
- cutlass (PCIe w/NUMA): 440 tok/s per GPU

Samira G: What about quantization experiments? Did int8 help on PCIe vs SXM differently?

Alex R: We did a calibrated int8 run using our layered-quant pipeline: int8 gave ~1.6x throughput on both topologies when kernels supported it. On PCIe the relative gain sometimes higher because compute bound part becomes dominant over bus transfer. Quality delta: logprob MLL increased by ~0.6% (acceptable for most infra configs).

Jin W: Any region-level variance beyond CPU/GPU SKU differences?

perf-bot: Region notes: eu-central1 increases p95 by ~10-15% vs us-west1 for same SXM SKU — traced to host NIC/driver differences and slightly older PCIe-to-NIC bridge firmware causing CPU stall jitter under high concurrency. Also observed that some cloud zones expose A100 PCIe variants with fewer PCIe lanes affecting throughput for heavy DMA patterns.

Olga P: For capacity planning: based on opt-13b traffic (avg prompt->gen 320 tok), 4x A100-SXM sustained ~2000 tok/s. For a 99th percentile latency SLO of 200ms and 40% headroom, we recommend sizing ~1 node per 1500 tok/s of steady load (so 4x A100-SXM per 1500 tok/s).

Alex R: Operational notes:
- Always enable NVLink-aware scheduling for sharded KV.
- For PCIe nodes, enforce CPU-GPU NUMA pinning by default for latency-sensitive workloads.
- Prefer cutlass+flash_attn stack on SXM for fp16; fallback to Triton fused for CPU-bound small-batch workloads.
- Run quick int8 QA on eval prompt sets before rolling quantized kernels.

Samira G: Action items?

Alex R: 1) eng-infra: add numactl pinning toggle to perf presets for PCIe instance family (Jin + Olga).
2) eng-runtime: expose kernel hinting per deployment (cutlass/triton priority) (Samira).
3) ml-evals: run int8 regression set on opt-13b across eu/us regions and post pass/fail (Alex).

Olga P: I'll open infra PR for numactl defaults and include a short doc snippet showing the `numactl` flags we used.

Jin W: I'll take the kernel hinting task.

Samira G: I'll schedule the int8 evals tomorrow and post results in this thread.

Alex R: Thanks all — tl;dr: SXM+NVLink wins for multi-GPU sharded inference; PCIe can be tuned with NUMA pinning and kernel choices to close the gap; watch region SKU differences for predictable capacity sizing. :thumbsup:
